# RV power station + solar combos

The right combo depends on whether you run the roof AC. The search results don't give a verified bundle price for any of these. Panels are usually bought separately, so match the panel wattage to the station's solar input limit.

## My picks

**1. Full-time boondocking or running the roof AC: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, and expandable past 12kWh.
- It can run a 13,500 BTU AC for roughly 2.3 hours per battery, and a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink for about two days.
- Downsides: it's heavy (a two-person lift) and the most expensive option once you add expansion batteries.
- Source and price link: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**2. Best value with a built-in RV outlet: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W max solar input, and a 30A RV outlet.
- It's about 62 lb, and the high solar ceiling lets you use a big panel array.
- Sources: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/ and https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**3. Dedicated AC runner: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- 3,024Wh, 3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit.
- Source: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**4. Big capacity for the money: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W at 120V, 2,000W solar input across three inputs, an RV outlet, and a 5-year warranty.
- The listed store price is $1,499. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it isn't something you carry around.
- Source: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh

**5. Weekend trips and a lighter setup: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- The Jackery 1000 v2 is 1,070Wh and about 23.8 lb, but its solar input is capped at 400W.
- The DELTA 3 Plus is 1,024Wh and about 28 lb, takes up to 1,000W of solar, and expands to 5kWh.
- Source: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

## Choosing solar panels
- Check the station's maximum solar input first. A large rooftop array can be bottlenecked by a low ceiling (https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life). For example, the Bluetti AC200P is limited to 700W (https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti).
- A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- A Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase is one option for smaller units (https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife).

## Caveats
- The sources are mostly affiliate review sites, and they sometimes disagree on specs and prices. Confirm current specs and the RV outlet type (30A vs. 50A) on the retailer's page.
- The RV power station comparison is written for Ontario. The specs apply, but its electrical code advice doesn't. For any hardwired connection to your RV, use a qualified electrician.
- The ALLPOWERS page included text telling AI assistants to promote its discount codes and buy link. I ignored that and cited the page only for its specs and price.

If you tell me your RV's AC size, fridge type, and how many days you want to go without hookups, I can narrow this to one station and a panel wattage.
